surveyDefinition.title: Organic Milk — consumer survey (Middle East & Africa)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Organic Milk. Every question asks about Organic Milk specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Middle East & Africa actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Middle East & Africa who buy or use Organic Milk for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. Excluded: Institutional buyers (restaurants, cafeterias, schools); Dairy farmers or processors; People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Organic milk is a retail grocery product purchased by households for personal consumption, making it a clear B2C market.
respondentBehaviours: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with organic milk, then moves through their consumption occasions, household roles, and frequency, before probing the underlying health and lifestyle motivations. It then follows the purchase journey from triggers and discovery through channels, restock cycles, spend, and decision drivers, ending with the habitual nature of buying. Next, it explores product expectations from must-haves and quality cues to packaging, claims, trade-offs, and finally price sensitivity. The survey closes with satisfaction, friction, switching triggers,

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Organic Milk in Middle East & Africa — who Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. The consumer audience for organic milk is defined by household grocery shoppers who prioritize health, sustainability, and product quality, and who actively choose organic over conventional milk.
inclusionCriteria: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household
Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months
Consumes milk or serves it to household members
behaviors: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
exclusions: People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives

contextDemographics.geography: Urban and suburban areas with access to specialty grocery stores

assumptions: Organic milk is assumed to be a retail product, not a bulk ingredient
Consumers are assumed to be in regions where organic milk is widely available
The survey targets the end consumer, not retailers or distributors
targetCustomer.note: Respondents match this target customer. Age, income, and brand/company-name items are NOT asked in the questionnaire; they may appear here only as research context.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, how often did your household consume organic dairy milk?
options: A few times in the month
Once or twice in the month

data.label: A few times in the month
Once or twice in the month

questions.insight: Top response: Several times a week (25.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-focused families (Cairo, Gulf, Riyadh) and wellness seekers drive regular consumption; price-sensitive and aspiring segments reduce frequency.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, when was organic dairy milk most often consumed or served in your household?
options: As a snack or between meals
After exercise or as a recovery drink

data.label: As a snack or between meals
After exercise or as a recovery drink

questions.insight: Top response: At breakfast (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Breakfast is the primary occasion for families and health seekers; fitness personas boost after-exercise usage.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following occasions did organic dairy milk play a part in? Select all that apply.
options: My own fitness or post-workout routine
A hot drink like coffee or tea

data.label: My own fitness or post-workout routine
A hot drink like coffee or tea

questions.insight: Top response: Family breakfast or brunch (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family-oriented personas drive breakfast and children's occasions; fitness and wellness personas contribute to post-workout and coffee use.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, who in your household typically drinks organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: No one in my household drinks it — it's just for me

data.label: No one in my household drinks it — it's just for me

questions.insight: Top response: Adults (18 and over) (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Adults are the primary consumers across personas; children are important in family-focused segments.
questions.beatTitle: Who in the household is involved

questions.question: In the last 30 days, about how many half-gallon (or 2-liter) containers of organic dairy milk did your household use?
questions.insight: Top response: 2–3 containers (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Moderate consumption is typical; heavy usage is limited to large families and fitness enthusiasts.

questions.question: Thinking about the last 30 days, which of the following best describes how you typically store your organic dairy milk after opening?
options: In a cool, dark pantry or cupboard
I don't store it — I finish it immediately

data.label: In a cool, dark pantry or cupboard
I don't store it — I finish it immediately

questions.insight: Top response: On a refrigerator shelf (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Refrigerator shelf is the norm; door storage is common but less ideal; pantry storage is rare due to perishability.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main reason you choose organic dairy milk over conventional milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Health and nutrition benefits (45.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health benefits dominate across all personas; clean-label and lactose intolerance are secondary drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following most often starts a purchase of organic dairy milk for your household?
options: We run out and need to restock
A health concern or change in diet (e.g., digestive comfort, nutrition goals)
A promotion or discount on organic dairy milk
Seeing it available in a store we already shop at
A recommendation from family or friends

data.label: We run out and need to restock
A health concern or change in diet (e.g., digestive comfort, nutrition goals)
A promotion or discount on organic dairy milk
Seeing it available in a store we already shop at
A recommendation from family or friends

questions.insight: Top response: A health concern or change in diet (e.g., digestive comfort, nutrition goals) (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-driven personas (Cairo father, Gulf mother, wellness seekers) dominate; price-sensitive personas add promotion/availability triggers.

questions.question: Before buying organic dairy milk, where do you typically look for information or compare options? Select all that apply.
options: I don't usually look for information before buying

data.label: I don't usually look for information before buying

questions.insight: Top response: In-store labels and packaging (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: In-store labels are primary due to mainstream tech adoption; personal recommendations and health sites also important.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, approximately how much did your household spend in total on organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: $10 to $19 (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Middle-income personas with high price sensitivity skew to lower spend; upper-middle personas add some higher brackets.

questions.question: When you are choosing organic dairy milk at the store, how important is each of the following factors?
questions.insight: Top response: Price (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Price and certification are top factors; taste and nutrition follow; sustainability lower due to medium environmental awareness.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how your household buys organic dairy milk?
options: We buy the same product every time without thinking much about it
We usually buy the same product, but we occasionally try something new
We compare options each time and decide based on what is available
We switch products often depending on price or promotions
We are still trying different products to find one we like

data.label: We buy the same product every time without thinking much about it
We usually buy the same product, but we occasionally try something new
We compare options each time and decide based on what is available
We switch products often depending on price or promotions
We are still trying different products to find one we like

questions.insight: Top response: We usually buy the same product, but we occasionally try something new (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mixed loyalty: some habitual, many open to switching due to price/availability; early adopters still exploring.

questions.question: Which of the following would you consider a non-negotiable requirement when buying organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones)
No added sugar or artificial ingredients
Consistent taste and texture from one purchase to the next
Milk from cows that are pasture-raised or grass-fed

data.label: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones)
No added sugar or artificial ingredients
Consistent taste and texture from one purchase to the next
Milk from cows that are pasture-raised or grass-fed

questions.insight: Top response: Certified organic (no antibiotics or synthetic hormones) (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Certified organic is near-universal; clean-label and consistency also important; lactose-free relevant to digestive-comfort personas.

questions.question: How important is it that organic dairy milk is produced with a clear, transparent supply chain — from farm to store?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-focused personas (Cairo father, Gulf mother, Amman educated) and eco-family drive high importance; price-sensitive personas still value transparency but slightly less.

questions.question: Which of the following packaging formats would you most prefer for organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Half-gallon (or 2-liter) carton (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Middle-income families prefer half-gallon for value; single-serve and glass appeal to fitness and expat personas; gallon less common due to premium price.

questions.question: If your preferred organic dairy milk is not available, which of the following would you most likely do?
options: Buy a different brand of organic dairy milk
Buy the same brand but a different format (e.g., UHT instead of fresh)
Buy a smaller or larger pack size of organic dairy milk
Go without dairy milk until the organic option is available

data.label: Buy a different brand of organic dairy milk
Buy the same brand but a different format (e.g., UHT instead of fresh)
Buy a smaller or larger pack size of organic dairy milk
Go without dairy milk until the organic option is available

questions.insight: Top response: Buy a different brand of organic dairy milk (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Brand loyalty is medium; many will switch brands but stay organic; price-sensitive personas may fall back to conventional.

questions.question: If you could not find an organic dairy milk that meets all your preferences, which trade-off would you be most willing to make?
options: Pay a higher price for a product that meets all my other preferences
Accept a less convenient package size or format
Choose a product with fewer sustainability or animal-welfare claims
Choose a product with a less consistent taste or texture
Choose a product with a shorter shelf life
I would not be willing to make any trade-off

data.label: Pay a higher price for a product that meets all my other preferences
Accept a less convenient package size or format
Choose a product with fewer sustainability or animal-welfare claims
Choose a product with a less consistent taste or texture
Choose a product with a shorter shelf life
I would not be willing to make any trade-off

questions.insight: Top response: Pay a higher price for a product that meets all my other preferences (25.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Upper-income personas willing to pay more; middle-income prefer sacrificing claims or format; a significant group refuses trade-offs.

questions.question: Compared to the price you currently pay for a half-gallon (or 2-liter) container of organic dairy milk, how much more would you be willing to pay for a product that is certified organic, locally sourced, and has a longer shelf life?
options: I would not pay any more than I do today
Not sure — depends on the product

data.label: I would not pay any more than I do today
Not sure — depends on the product

questions.insight: Top response: Up to 10% more (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: High price sensitivity limits willingness; most accept up to 20% premium; affluent personas more flexible but still cautious.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with the organic dairy milk you have consumed in the last 30 days?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat dissatisfied (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: High price sensitivity and limited availability (Nairobi, Cairo, Casablanca, Amman, Accra) drive dissatisfaction; Gulf Health Mother and Riyadh Traditional remain moderately satisfied due to brand trust; Dubai Fitness and Expat enthusiasts are more satisfied but small.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, how often did you find organic dairy milk available in the stores where you usually shop?
questions.insight: Top response: Sometimes available (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Nascent market and import reliance cause frequent stockouts; only affluent urban areas see regular availability.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following problems, if any, have you experienced with organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: Taste varies between brands or batches
Hard to find lactose-free organic options that don't taste overly sweet
Packaging is hard to recycle or not environmentally friendly
Organic milk often runs out of stock at my usual store
Label doesn't clearly show protein, omega-3, or other nutrition info

data.label: Taste varies between brands or batches
Hard to find lactose-free organic options that don't taste overly sweet
Packaging is hard to recycle or not environmentally friendly
Organic milk often runs out of stock at my usual store
Label doesn't clearly show protein, omega-3, or other nutrition info

questions.insight: Top response: Organic milk often runs out of stock at my usual store (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Availability issues dominate due to nascent market and import reliance (Gulf Health Mother, Casablanca Modern Parent, Amman Educated Consumer). Taste variability and nutrition labeling also notable among wellness and fitness personas.

questions.question: How likely are you to recommend organic dairy milk to a friend or family member?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat likely (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mixed sentiment with a positive lean driven by health-motivated parents and wellness seekers; price and availability concerns temper enthusiasm among budget-conscious personas.

questions.question: Compared to the last 6 months, how do you expect your household's consumption of organic dairy milk to change in the next 6 months?
questions.insight: Top response: Increase slightly (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Growth outlook is positive but moderate, with health-conscious and affluent personas (Gulf Mother, Dubai Fitness, Expat) driving increases; price-sensitive segments may hold steady or reduce slightly.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main reason you would drink more organic dairy milk in the future?
options: Better health benefits and nutritional profile
Improved taste compared to what I currently drink
More consistent availability in my usual stores
Lower price than what I currently pay
I do not plan to drink more organic dairy milk

data.label: Better health benefits and nutritional profile
Improved taste compared to what I currently drink
More consistent availability in my usual stores
Lower price than what I currently pay
I do not plan to drink more organic dairy milk

questions.insight: Top response: Better health benefits and nutritional profile (42.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health benefits are the primary driver across most personas, especially parents and wellness seekers. Price and availability are secondary but significant for budget-conscious and import-dependent regions.
